chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect of rs4784227; the association reflects a linked causal variant or a passenger regulatory change
predictions: rs4784227 does not itself alter allele-specific TF binding or enhancer activity in the relevant breast-cancer cell type.
The breast-cancer association is explained by linkage disequilibrium with another causal variant at 16q12.

FOXA1 occupancy at the element (E07) is not allele-specific and does not mediate a TOX3 expression change; absence of a breast-mammary eQTL (E09) and absence of an MCF7 ESR1 peak (E08) are consistent with no direct allelic mechanism.
falsified_if: A robust allele-specific TF-binding difference at rs4784227 is demonstrated in breast-cancer cells.
The variant itself reproducibly changes enhancer activity and TOX3 expression in a relevant context.
The allelic effect tracks the breast-cancer risk allele after controlling for linked variants.

chains.title: Alt T may increase FOXA1 binding at a distal enhancer, altering TOX3 expression and breast-cancer risk

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies the rs4784227-containing element in MCF7 (E07); the allele-specific direction, alt T binding more strongly than ref C, remains a prediction rather than a demonstrated effect.

rs4784227 lies within a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E3180851) with H3K27ac signal, consistent with an enhancer context; E03 z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples and do not establish MCF7-specific or allele-specific activity.
TOX3 is the closest protein-coding gene and the leading L2G target, but E09 finds no significant GTEx breast-mammary eQTL for this variant, so an effect on TOX3 expression is not demonstrated.

MCF7 is a relevant context because a FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak contains the variant in MCF7 (E07) and the breast-cancer GWAS/L2G evidence supports ER-positive/luminal relevance (E05), although E06 is title-level only.
The T allele is associated with increased breast-cancer risk in the strongest breast-cancer GWAS entries.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP-qPCR in MCF7 or another heterozygous ER-positive breast-cancer line shows higher FOXA1 signal on the alt T allele.
An enhancer reporter with the T allele has higher activity than the C allele in MCF7, and this difference is reduced by FOXA1 depletion.
FOXA1 knockdown reduces the allele-specific enhancer or expression effect at this locus.
falsified_if: No allele-specific FOXA1 binding is detected at rs4784227 in breast-cancer cells.
The T allele does not increase enhancer activity or TOX3 expression in a relevant context.
The allelic effect persists unchanged after FOXA1 knockdown.

chains.title: Alt T may increase ESR1/ER-alpha binding at the enhancer, altering TOX3 expression in ER-positive breast cancer

links.claim: Alt T binding ESR1 more strongly than ref C is proposed but unsupported; no allele-specific ESR1 data are available, and no ESR1 ChIP-seq peak contains the variant in MCF7 (E08).
rs4784227 lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E3180851), so an allele-specific ESR1 effect could alter enhancer activity if ESR1 bound there; this is not shown.
TOX3 is the closest and leading L2G gene, but E09 finds no significant GTEx breast-mammary eQTL for this variant, so an ESR1-dependent change in TOX3 expression is unproven.
ER-positive breast cancer is relevant from GWAS subtype evidence (E05), but E08 does not support ESR1 occupancy at this element in MCF7, and E06 is title-level only.
The T allele is associated with increased breast-cancer risk in the strongest breast-cancer GWAS entries.

predictions: Allele-specific ESR1 ChIP-qPCR in MCF7 or another ER-positive line shows higher ESR1 signal on the alt T allele.
The enhancer or expression effect is stronger in ER-positive breast-cancer cells and is reduced by ER antagonist treatment.
ESR1 depletion reduces any allele-specific enhancer effect.

TOX3 expression is not altered by ESR1 manipulation in this context.

chains.title: Ref C may strengthen CTCF binding at the enhancer, while alt T weakens CTCF and may alter TOX3 enhancer contact
chains.element: Distal enhancer EH38E3180851 (dELS) containing rs4784227, with a reported CTCF z-score in the cCRE registry

links.claim: Ref C binding CTCF more strongly than alt T is proposed but unsupported; E03 reports only a maximum CTCF z-score of 1.9 in the cCRE and provides no allele-specific CTCF binding data.
rs4784227 lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE with some CTCF signal (E03), but insulator function and allele-specific CTCF occupancy are not shown.
TOX3 is the nearest and leading L2G gene, but there is no evidence that CTCF loss on the T allele increases enhancer contact with TOX3, and E09 finds no breast-mammary eQTL.
Breast-cancer relevance is supported by GWAS/L2G evidence (E05), but MCF7-specific CTCF activity at this element is not shown; E06 is title-level only.
The T allele is associated with increased breast-cancer risk in the strongest breast-cancer GWAS entries.

predictions: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP-qPCR shows higher CTCF signal on the ref C allele than on alt T.
Alt T increases enhancer-promoter contact or TOX3 expression in a chromatin-contact assay.
CTCF depletion mimics the alt T allele's effect on TOX3 or chromatin contact.

Alt T does not increase enhancer contact or TOX3 expression.
CTCF depletion does not alter TOX3 expression or chromatin contact from this enhancer.

checks.why: Directly tests whether FOXA1 occupies the rs4784227-containing element in the stated expression context; a peak would support occupancy but not allele-specificity, while absence would weaken H1.binding and raise H4.
Directly tests whether ESR1 occupies the rs4784227-containing element in MCF7; an ESR1 peak would selectively support H2 over H1, while absence would weaken H2.binding.
Tests whether this variant is an eQTL for TOX3 in breast tissue, which would strengthen or weaken the gene links shared by H1/H2/H3 and help distinguish them from the null/linked-variant hypothesis.
